catalog.name: Cross-scenario model research
catalog.guidance: Use families as evidence-based research lenses, not a closed model menu. Confirm data semantics and time boundaries. Keep the host task objective, evaluation and resource budget fixed. A family with no upstream code is a documented concept, not an installed model.

families.name: Task framing and measurement
families.question: What decision is being optimized, at which stage, under which observable feedback?
families.experiment: Freeze the unit, target, split, metric, guardrails and comparison before selecting a model family.
families.pitfalls: A better proxy metric does not by itself establish a better downstream decision.

families.name: Collaborative retrieval
families.question: Can user-item co-occurrence recover useful candidates beyond a simple popularity baseline?
families.experiment: Compare neighborhood and factorization representations at fixed candidate count and retrieval metric.
families.pitfalls: Time leakage in interaction graphs and unseen-item support can invalidate the comparison.

families.name: Item embeddings and graph retrieval
families.question: Does item-context structure improve nearest-neighbor retrieval?
families.experiment: Compare co-occurrence, embedding and graph-aware item representations at matched retrieval budget.
families.pitfalls: Transductive embeddings can absorb evaluation-period interactions.

families.name: Two-tower matching
families.question: Does learned user-item matching improve recall within latency and index limits?
families.experiment: Compare a simple matching baseline with dot-product towers and assess recall, coverage and serving cost.
families.pitfalls: A matching score is not a calibrated treatment effect or business value.

families.name: Interest and sequence retrieval
families.question: Do multiple interests or event order improve retrieval?
families.experiment: Ablate pooled history, multiple interests and sequential attention using pre-cutoff event histories.
families.pitfalls: Aggregates cannot be expanded into event order; negative sampling must match the task.

families.name: Streaming retrieval and indexing
families.question: Is representation freshness or index maintenance limiting quality?
families.experiment: Compare fixed and updated representations with consistent latency, freshness and recall measurements.
families.pitfalls: Offline static data cannot validate online update consistency or service latency.

families.name: Feature representation and interactions
families.question: Which feature dependency is missed by the current representation?
families.experiment: Compare a fixed baseline with explicit or learned crosses and ablate the interaction component.
families.pitfalls: Capacity alone is not evidence for interaction benefit; use only available time-safe fields.

families.name: Behavior sequence ranking
families.question: Does recency, evolving interest or session structure improve target-conditioned prediction?
families.experiment: Compare static aggregates with time-safe sequential encoders and attention ablations.
families.pitfalls: Target-conditioned attention needs a real target representation; single-row aggregates are not sequences.

families.name: Multiple outcomes and task dependence
families.question: Can sharing across observed outcomes improve the fixed primary objective?
families.experiment: Compare separate heads, shared representations and gated experts with auxiliary-loss ablations.
families.pitfalls: Auxiliary labels and funnel dependencies must be observed; guard against negative transfer.

families.name: Scenario and context specialization
families.question: Do documented contexts have distinct response mechanisms?
families.experiment: Compare pooled and context-conditioned parameters with support and transfer checks.
families.pitfalls: Anonymous columns do not establish scenario meaning; small segments can overfit.

families.name: Slate reranking and diversity
families.question: Does joint selection improve relevance, diversity or constrained slate value?
families.experiment: Compare pointwise ordering with greedy or slate-aware selection at fixed candidate set and slate size.
families.pitfalls: A single binary action per user does not provide a slate or diversity target.

families.name: Feedback bias and causal support
families.question: Could exposure or selection bias explain apparent model quality?
families.experiment: Compare naive estimates with a design-appropriate correction and inspect support/variance.
families.pitfalls: A logged probability does not prove exchangeability; response scores are not effects.

families.name: Cold-start and sparse entities
families.question: Does performance fail on new users, items or sparse contexts?
families.experiment: Predefine cold-start cohorts and compare metadata/representation baselines on the same cohorts.
families.pitfalls: Do not identify cold-start cohorts from post-outcome activity.

families.name: Generative representations and tokenization
families.question: Is a generative representation suitable for the available item and sequence contract?
families.experiment: Compare tokenization and sequence objectives with a fixed non-generative baseline.
families.pitfalls: Token design, catalog coverage and output validity must be measured before quality claims.

families.name: Scaling and hardware-aware architecture
families.question: Does scaling architecture improve quality at a feasible training and serving cost?
families.experiment: Measure quality against parameters, FLOPs, memory, latency and sequence length.
families.pitfalls: A single larger run is not a scaling law; document compute and data budgets.

families.name: End-to-end generation for recommendation, search and ads
families.question: Can generation directly represent the target action or retrieved object?
families.experiment: Compare generated outputs with retrieval or ranking baselines under validity and cost constraints.
families.pitfalls: Generation cannot replace a missing action catalog, relevance labels or policy evaluation.

families.name: Semantic and reasoning recommendation
families.question: Does semantic alignment or explicit reasoning improve decisions beyond simpler representations?
families.experiment: Ablate semantic alignment and reasoning steps against matched model/compute baselines.
families.pitfalls: Unverifiable rationales are not evidence of better recommendations.

families.name: Diffusion augmentation and recommendation
families.question: Does diffusion-based augmentation or representation help under the actual data distribution?
families.experiment: Compare with non-diffusion augmentation while auditing generated sample validity.
families.pitfalls: Synthetic interactions must not be treated as randomized outcomes.

families.name: Offline-online system lifecycle
families.question: Which offline gain survives retrieval, feature freshness and serving constraints?
families.experiment: Check replay, feature parity, latency and deployment guardrails at a fixed model choice.
families.pitfalls: Offline benchmark success does not establish online production effect.

method_cards.mechanism: Forms elementwise products for feature pairs, learns an attention weight for each pair, pools them, and adds an optional linear logit.
method_cards.comparison: On the same split and fields, replace learned pair attention with uniform pair pooling while retaining the linear term and embedding width.
method_cards.failure_signals: No held-out gain over uniform pooling, or attention concentrates on unstable rare pairs.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec supplies a TensorFlow pointwise builder; the transferable idea is pair weighting, not its training code or a causal effect estimate.

method_cards.mechanism: Each APG layer uses a scene embedding to generate its central low-rank transformation while surrounding projections can be shared across scenes.
method_cards.comparison: On the same split, hold layer widths fixed and replace the scene-conditioned generated matrix with one shared matrix.
method_cards.failure_signals: No gain within sufficiently supported scenes, or gains vanish on held-out scene slices.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec implements an APGLayer-based ranker; using the idea elsewhere requires meaningful scene IDs and a new adapter.

method_cards.mechanism: Stacks multi-head self-attention over field embeddings so the representation of each field can depend on other fields before prediction.
method_cards.comparison: On the same split and embeddings, remove the attention interaction stack and feed pooled fields to the same prediction head.
method_cards.failure_signals: No gain over pooled fields at matched parameter and latency budgets.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec provides a field-attention TensorFlow ranker; this card proposes a controlled interaction experiment, not source-code reuse.

method_cards.mechanism: Combines a user-factor/item-factor dot product with learned user, item, and global bias terms; the source then applies a sigmoid prediction head.
method_cards.comparison: On the same interaction split, remove only the three bias terms from the factor model while keeping factor dimension and classifier head fixed.
method_cards.failure_signals: Biases do not improve held-out ranking or merely encode popularity without cohort gains.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec's executable is a TensorFlow pair classifier with exportable towers; its latent-factor comparison does not imply calibrated rating prediction.

method_cards.mechanism: A cross network repeatedly combines the original input with the current state to form explicit bounded-degree crosses, alongside a deep MLP branch.
method_cards.comparison: On the same split and fields, turn off only the cross branch while retaining the deep branch and linear features.
method_cards.failure_signals: No out-of-sample gain or the cross branch raises latency beyond the fixed budget.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec supplies its own DCN TensorFlow layer; transfer the cross-branch hypothesis, not a claim that every input cross is useful.

method_cards.mechanism: Adds an FM second-order embedding interaction logit to a DNN branch and an optional linear term using the same field inputs.
method_cards.comparison: On the same split and shared embeddings, remove only the FM branch while keeping the DNN and linear term fixed.
method_cards.failure_signals: The explicit second-order branch brings no held-out lift after capacity is controlled.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec's executable ranker is task-specific; its transferable question is whether second-order crosses add value beyond the deep branch.

method_cards.mechanism: A GRU extracts behavior states, optionally learns from next-behavior positive/negative auxiliary pairs, then target-conditioned attention controls a second interest-evolution GRU.
method_cards.comparison: On the same temporal split, disable only the auxiliary next-behavior loss while keeping the GRU evolution and target attention fixed.
method_cards.failure_signals: Auxiliary supervision yields no held-out gain or temporal leakage appears in sampled next behaviors.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec includes AIGRU, AGRU, and AUGRU variants; the comparison uses its optional auxiliary path and does not turn row aggregates into events.

method_cards.mechanism: Computes target-aware attention over a user's historical item embeddings and appends the weighted history representation to ordinary ranking features.
method_cards.comparison: On the same temporal split, replace target-aware history attention with a masked mean of the identical prior events.
method_cards.failure_signals: No gain versus history pooling or attention uses events after the candidate decision.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec implements a pointwise DIN builder with paired target/history feature columns; the target-conditioned mechanism requires real candidate items.

method_cards.mechanism: Encodes behavior within sessions using multi-head attention, models interactions among session summaries with a bidirectional LSTM, and activates both views against the target item.
method_cards.comparison: On the same temporal split, remove only the inter-session LSTM while retaining session boundaries, intra-session attention, and target activation.
method_cards.failure_signals: No gain from session interaction or session boundaries cannot be defined before the decision time.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec expects explicit per-session feature slots; a transferable session hypothesis does not justify synthesizing sessions from aggregate rows.

method_cards.mechanism: Independent user and item MLP towers produce L2-normalized vectors, whose cosine similarity feeds a binary prediction layer.
method_cards.comparison: On the same user-item split, keep input fields and vector size fixed and replace the nonlinear towers with linear projections.
method_cards.failure_signals: No recall gain at a fixed candidate count, or serving/index cost exceeds the budget.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec exports both towers; adopting the representation requires an indexing and negative-sampling contract in the destination system.

method_cards.mechanism: Learns an item vector as an item-specific weighted sum of ID and side-feature embeddings, then scores it against a context-item embedding; separate helpers form graph-walk context pairs.
method_cards.comparison: On the same context-pair split, replace item-specific attention weights with an unweighted mean while retaining embeddings and negatives.
method_cards.failure_signals: No cold-item or recall gain, or shuffled context pairs perform as well as true pairs.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec's builder consumes prepared context pairs and has separate graph utilities; it does not supply a general end-to-end graph pipeline.

method_cards.mechanism: Learns click probability and post-click conversion probability in separate towers, and constrains joint click-conversion probability to their product.
method_cards.comparison: On the same impression split and inputs, replace only the product-constrained joint head with an unconstrained direct joint head.
method_cards.failure_signals: The product constraint does not improve joint-outcome calibration or fails on low-click slices.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec outputs click and joint probabilities; interpreting its internal conversion tower requires observed click and joint labels, not an arbitrary second target.

method_cards.mechanism: A squeeze-excitation block reweights fields; bilinear pair interactions are computed on both original and reweighted embeddings before a DNN.
method_cards.comparison: On the same split, remove only the squeeze-excitation path while retaining the original bilinear interaction branch and DNN.
method_cards.failure_signals: Reweighting brings no held-out gain over original bilinear interactions at the same latency target.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec provides the particular SENet and bilinear layers; the transferable idea is testing field reweighting with a controlled interaction baseline.

method_cards.mechanism: Computes a factorization-machine second-order interaction over field embeddings and optionally adds first-order linear logits.
method_cards.comparison: On the same split and fields, set the FM interaction contribution to zero while keeping the first-order term and loss fixed.
method_cards.failure_signals: Second-order interactions provide no held-out lift or rely on post-decision fields.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec wraps the FM term in a binary ranking head; its source is an executable example, not a reusable cross-scene evaluation harness.

method_cards.mechanism: Factorizes an FM-like matching score into a user vector of a constant plus summed user embeddings and an item vector of item linear/item-item interaction terms plus summed item embeddings.
method_cards.comparison: On the same user-item split, remove only the item-side FM interaction scalar while holding vector width and recall protocol fixed.
method_cards.failure_signals: No recall or coverage gain over the simpler dot-product towers, or item vectors cannot be indexed consistently.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec supplies explicit user/item towers for this decomposition; it is not a generic implementation of all FM cross terms.

method_cards.mechanism: Learns user and item latent ID vectors, takes their dot product, then uses a sigmoid classification head in the FunRec implementation.
method_cards.comparison: On the same interaction split, shuffle only training user IDs while keeping item IDs, labels, factor dimension, and evaluation users fixed.
method_cards.failure_signals: Latent factors do not improve held-out retrieval beyond popularity or collapse on sparse users.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec's executable is a pair classifier with separately exportable ID embeddings; the dot-product idea does not itself predict ratings.

method_cards.mechanism: Shared experts feed gated domain towers; a domain-weight network mixes their outputs with stop-gradient on cross-domain contributions before one binary prediction.
method_cards.comparison: On the same split and domain slices, disable only cross-domain tower contributions while preserving the shared experts and own-domain tower.
method_cards.failure_signals: Transfer adds no gain in low-support domains or damages well-supported domains.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: This is a single-output multi-domain builder. Its nonshared-gate branch repeats each gate result while filling tower inputs, so indexed towers consume the first gate mixture; reimplement and verify the intended routing before transfer.

method_cards.mechanism: Runs causal sequence blocks with projected query/key/value interactions, optional relative-position or time-interval bias, gated output projection, and next-item sampled-negative training.
method_cards.comparison: On the same next-item split and sequence length, add only time-interval bias to the dot-product block while holding depth, negatives, and compute budget fixed.
method_cards.failure_signals: Time bias gives no quality gain or increases training/serving cost beyond the agreed budget.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec offers configurable HstuLayer modes; timestamps are needed for the time-bias ablation, and one run cannot establish a scaling law.

method_cards.mechanism: Fits Gensim Word2Vec to ordered item histories using local context windows; the source forms a user vector by averaging the learned vectors of prior items.
method_cards.comparison: On the same temporal split and corpus, change only the Word2Vec context window from one item to the planned width while keeping vector dimension fixed.
method_cards.failure_signals: Context vectors do not improve recall, or chronology-shuffled histories perform equally well.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec's class is a Word2Vec wrapper and mean-pooling helper, not a complete retrieval trainer or a guaranteed skip-gram configuration.

method_cards.mechanism: Builds item-item cosine similarity from positive co-interaction counts and sums neighbor similarity across a user's previously interacted items.
method_cards.comparison: On the same temporal split and neighbor count, replace cosine-normalized item co-occurrence with raw co-occurrence counts using identical history cutoffs.
method_cards.failure_signals: No recall gain over popularity or popularity-dominated neighbors reduce catalog coverage.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec supplies a standalone positive-only ItemCF class; absent exposures are not negative preferences or randomized controls.

method_cards.mechanism: Creates task, expert, and scenario views; a scenario-generated meta unit weights experts for each task and a scenario-conditioned meta tower produces each task output.
method_cards.comparison: On the same split, replace only the scenario view supplied to meta attention and towers with a shared constant while keeping tasks and experts fixed.
method_cards.failure_signals: No gain across observed task-by-scenario cells or severe negative transfer in small cells.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec implements this multi-scenario multi-task builder; optional sequence input does not remove its need for real task labels and scenario context.

method_cards.mechanism: Dynamic-routing capsules turn one user history into several interest vectors; label-aware attention selects a target-relevant interest for sampled-softmax training.
method_cards.comparison: On the same next-item split, restrict the capsule count to one while keeping embeddings, negatives, and candidate set fixed.
method_cards.failure_signals: Multiple interests do not improve recall or merely duplicate one another.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec exports several user interest vectors for retrieval; target-aware attention is used in training and does not provide a free target at retrieval time.

method_cards.mechanism: Several shared experts process the same features; each task has its own softmax gate over experts followed by a task-specific prediction tower.
method_cards.comparison: On the same split and task labels, replace only task-specific gates with one shared gate while keeping experts and towers fixed.
method_cards.failure_signals: No primary-task gain or one task degrades materially from negative transfer.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec's MMoE code expects observed labels per output; gate diversity is a hypothesis to test, not evidence of causal task dependence.

method_cards.mechanism: Bi-interaction pooling compresses second-order embedding products into a vector that a DNN maps to a prediction, with an optional linear term.
method_cards.comparison: On the same split, replace only bi-interaction pooling with summed embeddings before the same DNN.
method_cards.failure_signals: No gain beyond simple pooled embeddings at comparable model size.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec gives a pointwise NFM builder; the comparison concerns interaction representation rather than a different optimizer or target.

method_cards.mechanism: EPNet gates input embeddings using prior context, and PPNet gates intermediate layers separately for each output head using another context view.
method_cards.comparison: On the same split, replace only EPNet's context-conditioned embedding gate with an identity gate while keeping PPNet and heads fixed.
method_cards.failure_signals: No slice-level gain from embedding personalization or gates collapse to constants.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec's EPNet/PPNet builder can emit multiple heads; a destination must supply real prior context and any auxiliary head labels it enables.

method_cards.mechanism: Stacks extraction levels with both task-specific and shared experts; task gates mix their own and shared experts while a shared gate feeds the next level.
method_cards.comparison: On the same split and tasks, tie task-specific expert weights across tasks while retaining expert slots, gates, and task towers.
method_cards.failure_signals: Task-specific experts do not improve the primary outcome or harm a secondary task.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec implements a particular CGC stack; its complexity is transferable only when several valid outcomes are observed.

method_cards.mechanism: A product layer constructs inner and/or outer products between field embeddings before a DNN and optional linear term.
method_cards.comparison: On the same split, disable only the outer-product path while retaining inner products, the DNN, and the same fields.
method_cards.failure_signals: Outer products add no held-out gain relative to their compute and memory cost.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec exposes inner/outer switches in its PNN layer; the card asks which product path helps under a fixed data contract.

method_cards.mechanism: Adds position embeddings to user and candidate-slate features, applies Transformer encoder blocks across positions, and softmax-normalizes position scores.
method_cards.comparison: On the same slate split and slate length, remove only cross-position Transformer attention while keeping position features and output normalization.
method_cards.failure_signals: No slate-metric gain over independent position scoring or benefits disappear after position-bias checks.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec implements a PRM scorer, not a diversity objective or a new candidate generator; candidate sets and labels must exist.

method_cards.mechanism: Per-position CTR and continuation heads score a slate; FPSA beam search proposes permutations and a second pass selects the preferred ordering.
method_cards.comparison: On the same slate split, fixed head predictions, and objective weights, compare FPSA beam size one with a larger beam size.
method_cards.failure_signals: A wider search brings no slate reward gain or raises inference cost beyond the limit.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec defines heads and an inference helper; training both heads needs aligned labels, and its example config alone does not prove that contract.

method_cards.mechanism: Position-aware causal self-attention encodes each item-history prefix for next-item prediction with sampled negative items.
method_cards.comparison: On the same temporal next-item split and negative sampler, replace only causal self-attention with a history mean at equal embedding width.
method_cards.failure_signals: Ordered attention does not outperform mean history or sequence shuffling leaves quality unchanged.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec supplies a sequence training graph and item-vector evaluator; it needs ordered histories rather than one aggregate row per user.

method_cards.mechanism: Builds short-term interest with LSTM, self-attention, and user attention; separately pools long-term behavior and gates both into a retrieval vector.
method_cards.comparison: On the same next-item split, replace only learned short/long gated fusion with a fixed mean while preserving both history encoders.
method_cards.failure_signals: Learned fusion gives no recall gain or the short-history window leaks the target event.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec's SDM builder uses distinct short and long history feature groups and sampled softmax; transfer needs those histories to be defined.

method_cards.mechanism: One shared MLP representation feeds a separate prediction tower for every observed task.
method_cards.comparison: On the same split and task labels, compare the shared representation with separate per-task MLPs at a matched parameter budget.
method_cards.failure_signals: Sharing does not improve the primary task or causes measurable negative transfer.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec provides a multi-output TensorFlow baseline; its outputs require distinct measured labels and fixed task definitions.

method_cards.mechanism: Domain-partitioned normalization and a star-topology FCN combine shared and domain-specific transformations; an auxiliary domain-aware branch also contributes to the logit.
method_cards.comparison: On the same split and domains, replace domain-partitioned normalization with shared normalization while retaining the star FCN and auxiliary branch.
method_cards.failure_signals: No improvement on supported domains or small-domain calibration worsens.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec requires a discrete domain feature for this builder; anonymous columns do not establish valid scenario membership.

method_cards.mechanism: Scores item pairs through pairs of common users, downweighting active users and user pairs with many shared items before neighbor aggregation.
method_cards.comparison: On the same temporal split and neighbor count, remove only Swing's active-user downweighting while retaining its user-pair overlap denominator.
method_cards.failure_signals: No gain on held-out retrieval or sparse pairs make the similarity estimate unstable.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec's standalone Swing class uses positive interactions and at least two common users per scored pair; it does not infer counterfactual preference.

method_cards.mechanism: Builds user-user cosine similarity from positive shared-item counts, then recommends items interacted with by a user's nearest neighbors.
method_cards.comparison: On the same temporal split and neighbor count, replace cosine-normalized user co-occurrence with raw common-item counts using identical history cutoffs.
method_cards.failure_signals: No recall gain over popularity or neighbor coverage collapses for sparse users.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec provides a standalone positive-only UserCF class; lack of exposure cannot be interpreted as negative feedback.

method_cards.mechanism: Adds a linear wide term and configured explicit cross logits to a deep feature-embedding MLP before binary prediction.
method_cards.comparison: On the same split and deep branch, remove only configured explicit cross logits while retaining the linear wide term.
method_cards.failure_signals: Manual crosses provide no held-out lift or depend on unavailable/post-decision fields.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec executes configured crosses in a pointwise ranker; cross definitions must be redesigned for the destination schema.

method_cards.mechanism: Combines a compressed interaction network that explicitly creates vector-wise high-order crosses with a DNN branch and optional linear term.
method_cards.comparison: On the same split, remove only the CIN branch while keeping the DNN, linear term, and embedding inputs fixed.
method_cards.failure_signals: High-order crosses add no held-out gain or exceed the latency budget.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec's CIN implementation is an executable ranking component; the portable claim is a controlled high-order interaction test.

method_cards.mechanism: A DNN maps user features and optional pooled history to a normalized user vector; sampled softmax trains it against an item embedding table.
method_cards.comparison: On the same next-item split, remove only pooled history from the user tower while keeping item vectors, negatives, and retrieval K fixed.
method_cards.failure_signals: History adds no recall or gains vanish when targets are excluded from pre-cutoff history.
method_cards.implementation_boundary: FunRec exports user and item embeddings for evaluation; applying them needs a matched item index and sampled-softmax target contract.

steps.hypothesis: The conversion effect surface contains interactions/thresholds that a per-arm additive linear ridge cannot represent; estimating the effect directly by residualizing out a shared outcome surface with a nonlinear torch head will rank the top-20% policy better than the seed's linear T-learner.
steps.expected_result: Selected top-20% (3381 units, ~0.03 predicted cost per unit) mean conversion effect above the seed's 0.003312 with the paired-vs-random 95% lower bound remaining positive, and AUUC/Qini not below the seed values (0.00685/0.00253).
steps.approach: Replace the additive linear T-learner with a residualized direct-effect estimator: cross-fit a torch ridge outcome surface on the pooled randomized arms, then fit a torch MLP effect head on the Robinson/R-learner residual objective so capacity is spent on interactions in the effect surface instead of arm-level main effects. Cost model kept as the parent's linear ridge on the treated arm so the budget comparison is unchanged.

research.direction: Residualized direct-effect (R-learner) estimation with a nonlinear torch effect head, instead of two separate additive linear arm regressions
research.mechanism: Cross-fit a torch ridge outcome surface m(X) on the pooled randomized arms, then fit a torch MLP tau(X) on the residual objective (Y - m(X) - (T - p) * tau(X))^2 with weight decay, so model capacity models interactions in the effect surface rather than arm-level main effects.
research.why_now: The only evaluated candidate is an additive linear T-learner (top-20% mean effect 0.00331, SE 0.00082, paired-vs-random delta 0.00201), and no other effect-surface mechanism has been tested; READY feature_interactions methods remain untried.
research.data_rationale: All inputs are the declared pre-treatment fields V1..V7 with documented p=0.5 assignment, so centered arm residuals T - p are valid; cross-fitting keeps the nuisance surface from absorbing effect signal; preprocessing is fit on training rows only.
research.comparison: Same frozen split, features, objective, budget, and evaluator; only the estimator changes from per-arm linear torch ridge (parent seed) to a cross-fitted residualized direct-effect torch MLP head.
research.expected_result: Selected top-20% (3381 units, ~0.03 predicted cost per unit) mean conversion effect above the seed's 0.003312 with the paired-vs-random 95% lower bound remaining positive, and AUUC/Qini not below the seed values (0.00685/0.00253).
research.falsification: If the selected-20% mean conversion effect is at or below the seed's 0.003312, or the paired-vs-random interval's lower bound does not stay above zero, the nonlinear effect-surface hypothesis is not supported.

alternatives.direction: Keep the T-learner structure but give each arm a shared nonlinear outcome model certified on GPU
alternatives.mechanism: Fit one torch MLP outcome model per arm with weight decay and take the difference of arm predictions as tau(X), isolating nonlinearity from the change of estimand.
alternatives.reason: Closer to the parent estimator, so it separates the effect of capacity from the effect of residualization; reserved for a follow-up ablation if the direct-effect head helps.

alternatives.direction: Request per-row treatment timing and realized coupon cost records
alternatives.mechanism: Collect assignment timestamps for every declared field plus realized send and redemption cost per unit, then re-run the frozen policy with a time-gated feature set and a measured cost column.
alternatives.reason: Feature timing is declared only and the 0.15 send cost is assumed, so leakage and budget conclusions cannot be verified from the current data; a data request is needed before any online claim.

steps.expected_result: On the frozen validation split, the selected top-20% (3381 units, ~0.03 assumed cost per unit) mean conversion effect should exceed the seed's 0.003312 with the paired-vs-random 95% lower bound > 0; to support the added doubly robust correction over step-002, paired-vs-baseline against step-002 should be non-negative (mean >= 0) and AUUC/Qini should be at or above step-002's 0.007068/0.002750.
steps.approach: Crossover of step-002's per-arm nonlinear outcome models with step-001's direct-effect head and cross-fitting, plus the documented propensity in an augmented-IPW (AIPW) pseudo-outcome. For each outcome, 5-fold cross-fitting trains independent torch MLP outcome models on control and treated rows of the out-of-fold portion and predicts both mu0 and mu1 on the held-out fold, so nuisance overfitting cannot leak into the pseudo-outcome. The AIPW pseudo-outcome uses the documented e=0.5 (clipped), and a torch MLP effect head is fit on it with weight decay. Preprocessing (one-hot for low-cardinality fields, standardized continuous fields) uses train-only statistics; the cost model stays the linear treated-arm torch ridge used by both parents so the budget comparison is unchanged.

research.direction: Doubly robust augmented-IPW (AIPW) pseudo-outcome learning with cross-fitted per-arm nonlinear outcome models and a nonlinear effect head, instead of a pure difference of nonlinear outcome surfaces (step-002) or a shared-residual R-learner (step-001).
research.mechanism: For each arm, 5-fold cross-fit a torch MLP outcome model and predict out-of-fold mu0(X) and mu1(X) for every training row; form the AIPW pseudo-outcome psi = mu1 - mu0 + T(Y-mu1)/e - (1-T)(Y-mu0)/(1-e) with the documented e=0.5, then regress psi on X with a torch MLP effect head with weight decay. Cross-fitting keeps nuisance overfitting out of psi, and the propensity term explicitly corrects arm imbalance that a plain T-learner difference ignores.
research.why_now: Only three candidates exist: linear T-learner (seed 0.003312), residualized nonlinear R-learner (step-001 0.005323), and shared-trunk nonlinear T-learner (step-002 0.005560). step-002's reflection explicitly lists the AIPW pseudo-outcome learner with cross-fitted per-arm outcome models and documented propensity as the untested alternative, no candidate has used the propensity capability beyond a constant plug-in, and the feedback_bias family is ready.
research.data_rationale: All inputs are the declared pre-treatment fields V1..V7 with documented p=0.5 assignment, so arm indicators and the augmentation term are valid; one-hot/standardization statistics and all nuisance fits are computed on training rows only, and out-of-fold predictions keep the pseudo-outcome honest on the same frozen split.
research.comparison: Same frozen split, features, objective, cost budget, and evaluator as seed, step-001 and step-002; only the estimator changes from step-002's arm-selected-MSE difference of per-arm nonlinear surfaces and step-001's shared-residual effect head to an AIPW pseudo-outcome head built from cross-fitted per-arm nonlinear outcome models with the documented propensity.
research.expected_result: On the frozen validation split, the selected top-20% (3381 units, ~0.03 assumed cost per unit) mean conversion effect should exceed the seed's 0.003312 with the paired-vs-random 95% lower bound > 0; to support the added doubly robust correction over step-002, paired-vs-baseline against step-002 should be non-negative (mean >= 0) and AUUC/Qini should be at or above step-002's 0.007068/0.002750.
research.falsification: If the selected top-20% mean conversion effect is at or below the seed's 0.003312, or the paired-vs-random 95% lower bound is at or below zero, the AIPW effect head is not supported; if paired-vs-baseline against step-002 is negative with the 95% upper bound below zero (DR correction materially worse than the plain nonlinear T-learner), the added correction mechanism is rejected.

alternatives.direction: Residualized R-learner with a cross-fitted nonlinear nuisance instead of the linear ridge outcome surface.
alternatives.mechanism: Keep a single effect head on Robinson residuals but replace the cross-fitted torch ridge m(X) with a cross-fitted torch MLP outcome surface, so the residual objective sees a nonlinear baseline.
alternatives.reason: Directly tests whether step-001 was limited by nuisance misspecification rather than effect-head capacity, and isolates that from the new AIPW augmentation; deferred because it changes only the nuisance model inside an already-evaluated estimator.

alternatives.direction: X-learner two-stage imputation of individual treatment effects.
alternatives.mechanism: Fit outcome models per arm, impute treated-arm effects with the control model and control-arm effects with the treated model, then combine the two imputed effect regressions with the propensity as a weight.
alternatives.reason: Structurally different from both the residualized and AIPW heads and can help when one arm is harder to model, but it reuses the same per-arm nuisance fits as this candidate, so it is a follow-up ablation rather than the first test.

- Feature timing is declared only; there is no per-row evidence that V1..V7 are measured before assignment. The candidate remains testable because it only uses the declared fields as pre-treatment inputs, but a promoted policy would need row-level pre-treatment timestamps.

high.summary: 本报告为离线随机优惠券 uplift 实验。验证留出集 16907 人，预算为成本 0.03，成本按每位选中用户 0.15 的固定发券假设在全体评估用户上平均得到 0.029996；仅转化可用，活跃与净毛利不可用。before 候选（2091…）相对 random 的配对区间为正，且相对其基线 b5bf… 为正；after 候选（684e…）相对旧候选（2091…）的 paired_vs_baseline 转化均值为 -0.0022476，95% 区间 [-0.0037319, -0.0007633]，完全低于 0；相对 random 均值为 0.0020110，区间 [-0.0000496, 0.0040716] 含 0；AUUC/Qini 也低于 before。结论：在本次验证中，新候选未见可靠提升，且相对旧候选显著更差；但验证集可复用，配对区间不能作为最终提升证据。特征时点仅 manifest 声明，无法确认干预前测量。成本为固定发券假设，非实际核销成本。
high.recommendation: 建议不基于本次验证上线 after 新候选；优先保留旧候选/原基线，或回退到 before 旧候选，并暂停推广。若要继续迭代，先做独立复核：逐行核验 V1..V7 与干预时点、随机化概率与执行情况，并在未复用留出集上做确认实验；补充实际核销成本、净毛利与活跃标签（当前不可用）后再做成本-收益决策。不要用验证集区间重叠或单独区间宣称最终提升。

reflection.evidence: The candidate's actual objective score is 0.0033122375347489205, equal to the supplied baseline_score and not above the expected seed threshold of 0.003312; its selected top-20% conversion mean is also 0.0033122375347489205. The paired-vs-random 95% interval is mean 0.0020110013603832732 with lower -4.962340011673916e-05 and upper 0.004071626120883286, so the lower bound is <= 0, falsifying the expected >0 condition. More decisively, paired-vs-baseline against step-002 is mean -0.002247589755722482 with 95% interval [-0.003731853812722608, -0.0007633256987223558], entirely below zero, so the AIPW correction is materially worse than the plain nonlinear T-learner on this validation split. Ranking diagnostics are also below step-002: AUUC 0.006165274304125217 vs 0.007068, Qini 0.00184753608918466 vs 0.002750. error is null and there is no execution failure. The high/max analysis flags uplift_anomaly=true, cost_tradeoff_unclear=true, and feature_leakage flag=true but confirmed=false: feature timing is declared_only with no row-level pre-treatment evidence, assignment probability is documented but not independently audited, and cost is an assumed fixed 0.15 send cost averaged to 0.029996 rather than realized redemption cost. These limitations do not block the run or confirm leakage, so they do not make the result invalid, but they weaken causal/ROI interpretation. The tested claim was that the AIPW pseudo-outcome head with cross-fitted per-arm nonlinear outcome models and documented propensity would at least match step-002 and beat the seed; this claim was falsified for this configuration on this dataset and task. Untested alternatives remain: a cross-fitted nonlinear nuisance inside an R-learner, and X-learner two-stage imputation.
reflection.lesson: On this coupon dataset and task, the specific AIPW pseudo-outcome learner with cross-fitted per-arm MLP nuisances and a nonlinear effect head did not beat the seed and was materially worse than step-002's plain nonlinear T-learner, so the added doubly robust correction was not supported by this validation evidence. This does not generalize to all doubly robust, propensity-based, or AIPW methods; it only rejects this configuration under the observed frozen-split comparison. Validation gains are exploratory and not final proof; the lack of row-level feature-timing evidence, independent randomization/propensity audit, and realized cost/net-margin data further limits causal and ROI claims.
reflection.next_direction: Do not promote this candidate based on this validation result; retain or revert to step-002 or the seed. If continuing offline exploration, first independently audit row-level V1..V7 timing relative to assignment and verify executed randomization against the documented propensity, then test the remaining untested alternatives such as a cross-fitted nonlinear nuisance inside an R-learner or an X-learner imputation design, preferably on a fresh holdout or confirmatory split. Evaluate actual redemption cost, net margin, and active labels if they become available before making cost-benefit or business conclusions.

feature_request.definition: For every assignment unit, one row containing assignment_time and a measurement timestamp for each declared field V1..V7, so that each field can be checked to have been observed strictly before treatment assignment; optionally the same join may carry realized coupon redemption cost and net margin per unit for re-scoring under the cost budget.
feature_request.source: Experiment assignment/randomization log (unit_id -> assignment_time, arm) joined to the ETL/extraction records that produced V1..V7 for the same unit_id, plus the coupon ledger that records realized send and redemption amounts per unit.
feature_request.as_of: Per row, emitted with the same cutoffs used for the frozen training and holdout units: assignment_time and each feature's measurement_time recorded relative to assignment_time, with no post-assignment backfill or overwrite of the feature snapshots.
feature_request.evidence: Every validation report in history carries data_validation.feature_timing='declared_only' with the note that row-level time evidence is missing; the high and max reviews of seed, step-001, step-002 and step-003 all set feature_leakage flag=true, confirmed=false on exactly that basis, and cost_tradeoff_unclear=true because predicted_cost_per_unit equals the assumed 0.029996 rather than a realized cost. step-002's feature_gaps_md states verbatim that no per-row evidence exists that V1..V7 are measured before assignment and that realized redemption cost and net margin are absent from the frozen dataset.
feature_request.validation_plan: Join the new timestamps onto the frozen train/validation units and compute per feature the fraction of rows with measurement_time >= assignment_time; report any field that is not verifiably pre-assignment and drop it. Re-fit seed and the best candidate (step-002's shared-trunk per-arm nonlinear T-learner) on the verified field set under the identical split, objective, cost budget and evaluator, and compare paired-vs-random and paired-vs-baseline intervals plus AUUC/Qini against the archived prediction hashes. If realized cost per unit is present, recompute predicted_cost_per_unit and the selected-20% policy value against the 0.03 budget and check whether the observed cost interval still fits; if a field is dropped or cost changes the selected set, treat all earlier validation orderings as superseded.
